findings.title: The standard's done rule still says a deferral with a mitigation buys the next round with or without a commit
findings.description:
agents.md:42 still states the done rule from before this pull request: "a new correctness finding the shaper fixes, defers with a mitigation or asks about ... buys the next round whatever the answer and with or without a commit; a deferral that ships nothing buys none". The code no longer does this. `buys` (workflows/redline-loop.js:4132) is `own === 'fix' || (own === 'defer' && landed(id))`, so a deferral buys a round only when a commit of its own landed. docs/running.md:44 says the same ("A deferral buys a round only through a commit of its own").

On the base branch the standard was right. There, `buys(shaperOwn, shaperMitigated(id))` read the shaper's words, so a shaper deferral with a mitigation bought the round without a commit. This pull request changed the rule and rewrote agents.md lines 39, 46 and 49, but not this sentence. The line sits inside the diff's hunk (@@ -36,14 +36,14) as unchanged context.

The comment at workflows/redline-loop.js:4113-4116 ("in full, or by a deferral's mitigation ... whether or not a commit resulted") repeats the old rule. Its own continuation at 4125-4130 states the new one.
findings.proposedFix: Reword agents.md:42 so a deferral buys the next round only through a commit of its own (a planned mitigation the build left out buys nothing), citing #100. Reword the comment at workflows/redline-loop.js:4113-4116 the same way.

findings.title: No check pins an accept override beside a filled resolve entry, the neighbour R1-11's comment names
findings.description:
R1-11's fix (workflows/redline-loop.js:3816-3818) makes any override that names a disposition decide the matter. That covers `accept` as well as `fix`.

The new checks pin only the `fix` half: `overrideUnbuilt` and `overrideBuilt`, at 3151-3154. The comment at 3134-3135 names `deferAccepted` as the accept neighbour. But `deferAccepted` (2916) scripts no `resolveDeferred`, so it never puts a filled resolve entry beside an accept override. The plan-dial accept at 454 has none either. No other scenario combines the two.

Why a mutation survives:
- Suppose `if (decision.disposition) { return decision.disposition === 'defer' }` becomes `if (decision.disposition === 'fix') { return false }`.
- An accept override with a stray filled entry then falls through to `resolveDeferred.has(d.id) && (mitigationFilled(d) || ...)` (3819) and reads as a deferral, so it is filed and posted with `Deferred to #301`.
- No check covers that case.

I traced this through the code; I could not run the suite (node is not available to this role).
findings.proposedFix: Add an `accept` override scenario with `resolveDeferred: [{ id: 'R1-1', mitigation: 'a guard', ...draft }]`. Check that it files nothing, that `res.deferred` is empty, and that the reply is `Redline round 1: Keep it as it is. No code change. · decided by: @author`. Then correct the comment at 3134-3135 to name the new scenario.

findings.title: DEFERRED_SCHEMA's comment says the mitigation is never read to decide, but isDeferral decides from it
findings.description:
The comment on DEFERRED_SCHEMA (766-767, added by this pull request) says `mitigation` is "shown and never read to decide (#100)". `isDeferral` does decide from it. For a call's decision, `resolveDeferred.has(d.id) && (mitigationFilled(d) || !plannedTask(d.id))` (3819) reads a filled field as the person's deferral, which takes the finding out of `needCommits` and files a draft.

The comment on `mitigationFilled` (774-783) says correctly that this test has one reader, isDeferral. R1-7's fix rewrote that comment but not this one, so the two comments a few lines apart now disagree.
findings.proposedFix: Change 766-767 to say the words never decide what ships, and that the field is read once, as filled or empty, by isDeferral for a call's decision (#99). Or point to the mitigationFilled comment.

findings.title: The plan-dial stop returns a deferral's words when nothing is planned, against R1-7's new 'shown only beside a mitigation that ships'
findings.proposedFix: Narrow the comment at 777-778 and the docs/running.md sentence to the draft views (`drafts[].mitigation`, the result's `deferred[].mitigation`), saying the plan dial's `deferredPlanned` keeps the shaper's words. Or blank `deferredPlanned[].mitigation` where the finding's `files` are empty, as draftView does.

findings.title: FILES_ASK's 'an empty list when it has no task' gives an ask a different meaning from the ask-rules block's 'the paths its task would touch'
findings.description:
FILES_ASK (866, added by this pull request) asks every shape, human-pass and reshape prompt for "files (the paths its task creates or changes, an empty list when it has no task)". In a repository with ask rules, the same prompt also carries `rulesBlock` (517), which asks for "files, the paths its task would touch, so the workflow can apply the paths rules".

For an `ask` or a `decline`, which has no task in the plan, the two readings differ: an empty list by FILES_ASK, or the paths the recommended change would touch by the rules block.

The shaper's own file leans on both:
- rule 30 (agents/redline-shaper.md:30) says "the paths its task would create or change";
- its example R1-3 (line 41) lists `config/project/project.yaml` for an ask.

The loop test's scripted shaper returns `[]` for every ask and decline (tests/loop-test.mjs:227).

`forceAskRules` reads `[f.file].concat(files)` (3231) as its second check after the shaper's own tag. An ask returned with `files: []` whose recommended change writes under a `paths` rule, filed against another file and not tagged, is not forced to the person. On autopilot its recommendation is applied. After that, the plan approver's rule 5 or the guard refuses the write, which ends in a bounce or a blocked implementer, not in a write under the rule.

Whether a shaper returns `[]` here depends on how it reads the two sentences. The conflict itself is in the prompt text. #105 tracks the template example missing `files`, a different gap.
findings.proposedFix: Word FILES_ASK so it agrees with the rules block, for example "files (the paths its task creates or changes, or for an ask the paths its recommended change would touch; an empty list when there are none)".

findings.title: A person's deferral whose mitigation commit only mentions its id is replied to as 'No code change.'
findings.description:
`outcomesFor` now keeps a deferral's commits only when one is its own: `own = named.filter((c) => ownCommit(c, f.id))` (2937), `shipped = shipsNothing ? [] : named` (2939).

For a deferral the person or autopilot chose, the outcome is `kind: 'decided'` with `commits: shipped` (2949). `replyBody` then posts `<decision> No code change. Deferred to #<n>.` (1532) whenever no commit opens `redline: <id>` or was reported for the finding.

Case: a 'Mitigate' answer whose guard is committed as `redline: guard the queue for R1-1 (#100)` and not reported with `finding`. The guard is pushed with the round, and the thread says no code changed.

On the base branch, `shipped` for a decided deferral with filled words was `named` (mentions included), so the reply read `Applied in <sha>`. The pull request lists "posted as shipping nothing" for a mention-only commit as a deliberate change. The README's Known limits gives the cost as "named in no reply". The decided reply's text goes further and states that no code changed.

Conditions: the implementer commits the mitigation under a subject that does not open with the id and does not report it, against its rule 3 (agents/redline-implementer.md:18). Traced through the code; the suite could not be run here.
findings.proposedFix: For a decided deferral with no commit of its own, post the draft's destination without 'No code change.' when any round commit mentions the id. Or say the mention is not counted (for example `No commit of its own; Deferred to #301.`). Then align README Known limits with the wording chosen.

findings.title: The result's deferred entry reads empty words as 'nothing shipped', so the closing summary drops a mitigation that shipped
findings.description:
`deferredEntry` sets `mitigation: outcome.commits.length ? d.item.mitigation : ''` (3388), and the entry has no `ships` field.

Case: a shaper deferral with mitigation `''` and `files: ['app/x.php']` whose `redline: R1-1` commit lands. The PR's pinned mirror case, "a deferral worded none, or left empty, with a planned task with files and its own commit is posted as mitigated".
- The reply says `Mitigated in <sha>`.
- The result's entry carries `mitigation: ''`.

The skill's done and capped summaries (skills/redline/SKILL.md:264, 268) print "the mitigation that shipped, when one did (`mitigation` is empty when nothing shipped)". So the closing summary in the session lists R1-1 with no mitigation, although a reviewed commit shipped one. At this last step, the emptiness of the words decides what the summary shows, which goes against the pull request's "the words decide nothing".

The base branch had the same result through `hasMitigation('')`. This pull request rewrote the line and kept the behaviour.
findings.proposedFix: Add `ships: outcome.commits.length > 0` to the deferred entry, as `draftView` has, and have SKILL.md's done and capped sections read `ships` ("a planned change" when the words are empty), not the emptiness of `mitigation`. Pin it on the empty-words case with a commit of its own.

findings.title: An override to fix or accept keeps the resolve agent's stray deferred entry in the list the approver and the implementer are shown
findings.description:
`resolveWith` drops entries for findings changed away from defer: `deferred = deferred.filter((d) => !awayFromDefer(d.id))` (3729). It does this before the resolve agent runs. Afterwards it merges that agent's entries in, filtered only by `record.forced` (3749, 3771), so an entry the agent returns beside an override to fix or accept stays in `deferred`.

R1-11's fix makes `isDeferral` false for such an entry (3816-3818), so it is no longer filed or demanded. But the raw `deferred` still goes to:
- the plan approver (`{ findings: approverFindings(), deferred }`, 3851);
- the implementer (`ctx.deferred`, 3973, printed at 2161-2162 under "a defer task ships only the mitigation").

In R1-11's own scenario (tests/loop-test.mjs:3148-3154) both prompts list R1-1 with `"disposition": "fix"` beside `deferred: [{ id: 'R1-1', mitigation: 'a guard', ... }]`. That breaks the rule stated at 3696-3698 and in R1-11's new comment ("an override to fix or accept leaves no deferral behind (awayFromDefer), whatever entry the resolve agent returns").

What each agent then does turns on how it reads the contradiction:
- the approver may bounce over the stray entry;
- the implementer's rules send it to `plan.md`, which holds the full fix.
If a guard alone were committed as `redline: R1-1`, `needCommits` would be met and the reply would read `Fix it in full. Applied in <sha>`.

Conditions: the resolve agent returns an entry for an override that does not defer, which its prompt does not ask for (2053). The cause is at 3771, which this pull request did not change. #99 tracks a call's stray entry, not an override's.
findings.proposedFix: After the merge at 3771, filter again: `deferred = deferred.filter((d) => !awayFromDefer(d.id))`, with a warning naming the dropped entry. Or apply `awayFromDefer` to `fresh` before the merge. Pin it on `overrideBuilt`: the `plan approver r1` and `implement r1` prompts list no deferred entry for R1-1.

findings.title: shaperPlanned is redundant inside plannedFiles
findings.description:
`shaperPlanned` (3787) has one caller, `plannedFiles`' undecided branch, `shaperPlanned(id) ? shaperFiles(id) : []` (3793). In that branch `!roundDecisions[id]` already holds. `shaperFiles(id)` (3636-3639) returns the files of the shaper's defer finding with that id, or `[]`.

The ternary therefore equals `shaperFiles(id)`, except where the shaper returned two findings with the same id. Then `some` and `find` could disagree, an input the shaper's vetting is meant to exclude. The comment block at 3781-3786 explains an indirection that changes nothing.
findings.proposedFix: `const plannedFiles = (id) => (roundDecisions[id] ? unique(resolvedTasks.filter((task) => task.finding === id).flatMap((task) => task.files)) : shaperFiles(id))`. Then remove `shaperPlanned`, and fold its comment into plannedFiles' comment and the reference at 853.

findings.title: plannedFiles unions every resolve's tasks for a decided finding, so a replan that drops its task is never seen
findings.description:
For a finding the person or autopilot decided, `plannedFiles` is `unique(resolvedTasks.filter((task) => task.finding === id).flatMap((task) => task.files))` (3791-3792). `resolvedTasks` accumulates every resolve's tasks (3767). So once one resolve planned files for a decided deferral, a later resolve that plans none for the same id changes nothing.

Since R1-2's fix, this list is what the plan approver is shown for a decided deferral (`approverFindings`, 3798). The same list feeds:
- the planned-and-unbuilt warning (4055-4057);
- `ships` at a draft stop (3827, 3406).

Path:
1. R1-1 is overridden to defer behind a guard, and `resolve r1` plans `app/x.php`.
2. The plan bounces, the reshape returns a judgment call for R1-1, and `raised` (3876) counts it, since overrides are not in `calls`.
3. `resolve r1 #1` replans it with no task with files.
4. `plan approver r1 #2` is still shown `files: ["app/x.php"]`. The approver's rule 1 (agents/redline-plan-approver.md:16) bounces a defer whose files list has no task in plan.md, which can repeat until `maxPlanAdjustments`.
5. After the build, the warning says a mitigation was planned in app/x.php.

Conditions: a reshape that raises a call for an already-overridden finding, against the reshape prompt's "a decision the person made ... stays as it is" (2011), and a second resolve that drops the task. #97 R2-14 chose to read every resolve's tasks, for different calls; it did not consider the same id replanned. I traced this through the code; the loop test could not be run here.
findings.proposedFix: For a decided finding, read the tasks of the latest resolve that planned that id: keep tasks per id, with a later resolve's tasks for an id replacing an earlier one's, so tasks for other ids still accumulate as R2-14 requires.

findings.title: The implementer is still shown the shaper's files for a decided deferral's old disposition
findings.description:
R1-2's fix corrects only the plan approver's view (`approverFindings`, 3798). The implementer gets `ctx.shaped = { ...shaped, findings: finalDispositions }` (3973), and `finalDispositions` is `effectiveDispositions()` (3775-3778). That copies the shaper's finding and replaces only its `disposition`.

Example: a shaper fix with `files: ['app/x.php']` that the person changes to defer, with nothing shipping. The `implement r1` prompt (2161-2162) lists R1-1 as `"disposition": "defer", "files": ["app/x.php"]` beside a deferred entry with mitigation `''`, while plan.md has no task for it.

Because #100 makes `files` required, this stale list now reaches the implementer in every repository, not only those with ask rules.

No rule of the implementer reads `files`. Its file and the prompt send it to `plan.md` ("Every task says which files it touches; you touch those and nothing else", agents/redline-implementer.md:16; "a deferred finding with no task in plan.md gets no change and no commit", 2161). So the claim that it builds the abandoned fix rests on the implementer trusting the JSON over its rules. The contradiction in the prompt is real. The plan dial's list and any later reader of `finalDispositions` get the same stale list. The cause is in `effectiveDispositions`, which this pull request did not change.
findings.proposedFix: Carry the record's files on the finding in one place: in `effectiveDispositions()` (or a wrapper every prompt reads), set `files: plannedFiles(f.id)` for a decided deferral. The approver, the implementer and any later reader then share one list, and `approverFindings` can go.

findings.title: Whether a deferral's own commit landed is computed three times
findings.proposedFix: Compute the own commits once per finding: a map from id to its own commits, built from `roundCommits` beside `outcomes`. Read it in `outcomesFor`, `landed` and the warning.

accounting.ref: R2-11: the same cause, effectiveDispositions carrying the shaper's files for a decided deferral, fixed for the approver alone; this candidate names the general fix, given in R2-11's proposed fix
